── MARISOL'S WEEK ──
Marisol is training for a second marathon, the Wexley Lakes Marathon, aiming to break 3:45 after a 4:02 debut. Marisol runs five days a week, with a session on Wednesday, the long run on Sunday and Monday and Friday off, and ran about 30 miles a week before this build.
Recent weeks: 40, 42, 46, 34 mi
This week: 41 mi over 5 runs.
Raced: Sun Oct 18, 26.22 mi in 3h 50m
Pain noted: Sun 3/10 (Quads and calves very sore, normal marathon sore I think)
Body: "Quads are wrecked, stairs are hard. Blister on my left big toe."
Feeling: "Proud and tired."
Asks: "How long before I can run again? A friend wants me to race the Thanksgiving 10K in five weeks."

── THE DRAFT ──
Tells Marisol: A 3:50 marathon with a 12-minute PR is a real result, so this week is for walking, sleeping and letting the quads come back. …
Answers: (1) Give it a full week with no running. Walking is good, stairs and easy movement are good, and the quads will tell you when they are ready. (2) The Thanksgiving 10K on Nov 22 is 5 weeks out, which is on the edge. … (3) If the quads stay sore past about 10 days, or anything sharp shows up when you start jogging again, stop and see a sports physio before pushing on.
Safety flag: Watch the quads and the blister
Next week:
Mon: rest. Full day off; walk if you want, nothing structured.
Tue: other, 30 min walk, flat and easy, no running. Moves blood through sore quads.
Wed: rest. Protect sleep tonight more than anything.
Thu: other, 30 min walk, easy pace. Keep the legs loose without loading them.
Fri: rest. Let the week accumulate rest, not fitness.
Sat: easy, 2 mi, very slow jog only if quads feel normal walking stairs; otherwise walk…
Sun: easy, 3 mi, conversational and short, stop if anything pulls. Gentle…
